issues.quote: request lifecycle — the complete path one request takes: Kestrel, routing, every middleware in order
issues.text: Carried from r1, still unapplied. "complete" and "every middleware" overstate: the lab sets ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development (docker-compose.yml:93) and middleware8.md:5 (>= aspnetcore-8.0) says "UseDeveloperExceptionPage is added first when the HostingEnvironment is \"Development\"", so a framework-added middleware sits outside ExceptionHandlingMiddleware; the diagram's K->>M1 / M1-->>K is exact only for Program.cs's own middleware. s4 and summary 5 already scope to "middleware Program.cs registers"; s3 does not.
issues.fix: In s3 drop "complete" ("the path one request takes: ...") and change "every middleware in order" to "every middleware Program.cs registers, in order". Optionally add under the diagram: "The framework can add a few middleware of its own around these; this lesson follows only the ones Program.cs registers." Do not name DeveloperExceptionPage (scope).

issues.text: `curl`, `localhost` and (step 2) `docker compose` are tool/network names I have not been taught. Each is glossed inline by what the command does, so I can copy, run and check the result without stopping; I only do not know what the tools are.
issues.fix: No change required for this lesson; if a track lesson introduces curl/docker compose, link it in Before you start. Optionally add "(this machine)" after the first `localhost`.

issues.quote: and blocks until the app shuts down
issues.text: "Blocks" is jargon I do not have; I guess it means the line does not finish until the app stops. Side note, so it does not affect the main idea.
issues.fix: Replace "and blocks until the app shuts down" with "and does not return until the app shuts down".

issues.quote: Reading top to bottom names the forward order for these six calls: exception handling, logging, `UseCors`, `UseAuthentication`, `UseAuthorization`, then the matched endpoint.
issues.text: The block has seven `app.` lines; the sixth item is "the matched endpoint", not a call, and the previous paragraph said `app.MapControllers()` is not a step the response passes back through. I had to stop and work out whether `MapControllers` counts as one of the "six calls".
issues.fix: Replace "these six calls" with "these five calls and the endpoint" here and in "the reverse order of these six calls" in the next paragraph.

issues.quote: for every request the endpoint or `UseAuthorization` answers, whether it reaches `app.MapControllers()` or stops one line earlier, at `UseAuthorization`.
issues.text: Read this sentence twice. For a rejected request the way out is not "this list backward" in full, only the part from `UseAuthorization` back; the sentence packs both cases into one clause and I had to reconstruct that myself.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: "For a request the endpoint answers, that is the whole list backward. For one `UseAuthorization` rejects, it is the same list backward starting from `UseAuthorization`."

issues.quote: In what order does the response pass back through these calls, and who sees it last before the client?
issues.text: "Who sees it last" could mean the last middleware (`ExceptionHandlingMiddleware`) or Kestrel. The lesson answers both (section 4 last sentence; Connections), but never says which one the question meant, so I was unsure I had the intended answer.
issues.fix: Change to "which of these calls sees it last, before Kestrel sends it to the client?"

issues.quote: No — `ExceptionHandlingMiddleware` must be registered first among Đơn Hàng's own middleware, so nothing may run before it
